question.text: Lotus Capital AIF's investee, Saraswati Infra Ltd, has a pre-tax cost of debt of 10%, cost of equity of 18%, debt-to-equity ratio 1:1, and a tax rate of 30%. Compute the WACC used for DCF valuation.

explanation.text: The Logic: Post-tax cost of debt = 10% x (1 - 0.30) = 7%. With D/E = 1:1, weights are 50% debt and 50% equity. WACC = (0.50 x 7%) + (0.50 x 18%) = 3.5% + 9% = 12.5%. The Trap: 14.00% ignores the tax shield and uses pre-tax cost of debt; 11.00% uses wrong debt/equity weights; 12.00% uses a 20% tax rate instead of 30%. Tax-adjust only the cost of debt, since equity returns are not tax deductible to the firm. Note: The workbook supports WACC computed using post-tax cost of debt and cost of equity at capital-structure weights.
